title: The dua after eating with its meaning
intro: After eating we thank Allah for the food and drink He gave us.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: O believers, eat of the good things We have provided for you, and be grateful to Allah, if it is Him you worship. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:172)</small>
Muslims thank Allah in every situation – and also after eating, for the provision He gave. It is lovely to recite this dua after eating:

learn.label: The dua after eating
learn.ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ. كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ. الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
learn.tr: Bismillaahir-Rahmaanir-Raheem. Kuloo washraboo wa laa tusrifoo, innahoo laa yuhibbul-musrifeen. Al-hamdu lillaahil-ladhee at‘amanaa wa saqaanaa wa ja‘alanaa minal-muslimeen.
learn.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Eat and drink, but do not be excessive; He does not love those who are excessive. Praise be to Allah who gave us food and drink and made us Muslims.

learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) thanked Allah after eating and recommended that we make dua too. The dua does not have to be in Arabic – we can thank Allah in our own language as well.
Listen and repeat: Dua after Eating with the recording.

practice.title: The dua in order
practice.prompt: Put the parts of the dua in order.

questions.q: When do we recite this dua?
Must the dua be in Arabic?
options: No – we can thank Allah in our own language too
We don’t need to thank Allah
